Q: How to turn off Github Auto Code Suggestion on IntelliJ IDEA 2023.3.3 (Community Edition)? MacOS A:

I was also facing this same issue. I had disabled the option in GitHub Copilot's settings to show inline completions, but I was still seeing them. The following steps finally got rid of them for me, since it turns out they weren't coming from GitHub Copilot after all.

  1. Open Settings (Windows/Linux) or Preferences (macOS)

  2. Navigate to Editor→General→Code Completion→Inline

  3. Disable "Enable inline code completion using language models:"

Q: Get first non-empty cell that matches a value in VLOOKUP A:

Depending on the expected result format, the next formulas returns the required values:

The formula in C47 cell

=VLOOKUP(A47,FILTER(A$47:B$56,B$47:B$56>0),2,FALSE)

This filters the table on column B data greater then 0, and after does a VLOOKUP on the result for the actual Invoice Number

The other formula in cell E47

=HSTACK(UNIQUE(A47:A56),VLOOKUP(UNIQUE(A47:A56),IF((A47:A56*B47:B56)>0,A47:B56,""),2,FALSE))

is a spilling formula, which gets the unique Invoice Number and then makes the VLOOKUP on a table which contains only rows where both columns are filled with data. This is achieved with the multiplying of the columns and compare the result to >0 value.
The HSTACK arrange the unique Invoice Number and the VLOOKUP result to generate a table.

Q: Add case expression with calculations A:

When you are using CASE expression, both output of case should return same datatype otherwise it will end up with CAST error.

As @Larnu said, Implicit coversion will happen only for Int / Float not for Decimal, so when you are returning decimal in case expression then you need to cast explicitly otherwise return 0 or null.

In your case, CAST(LineTotal AS decimal(22,8)) /1.02 return NULL and else returns empty string, which causing the error

SELECT (CASE WHEN taxcode = 'NBT2' THEN (CAST(LineTotal AS decimal(22,8)) /1.02) 
             ELSE 0.0 END) 
FROM DPI1

Or

SELECT (CASE WHEN taxcode = 'NBT2' THEN (cast(LineTotal AS decimal(22,8)) /1.02) 
             ELSE NULL END) 
FROM DPI1

Q: CASE expression with boolean operator A:

This is the right format, also comparing varchar with the < symbol is quite odd,
maybe you will have to cast your weeks into integers first.
By the way, what if the week is over or equal than 53?

Also, you better use a corresponding table rather than hardcode the cases.

SELECT      t1.region, 
            Count(t1.orders) AS orders, 
            CASE 
                  WHEN t1.week < 5 THEN 'APR'
                  WHEN t1.week < 10 THEN 'MAY'
                  WHEN t1.week < 14 THEN 'JUN' 
                  WHEN t1.week < 19 THEN 'JUL' 
                  WHEN t1.week < 23 THEN 'AUG' 
                  WHEN t1.week < 27 THEN 'SEP' 
                  WHEN t1.week < 32 THEN 'OCT' 
                  WHEN t1.week < 36 THEN 'NOV' 
                  WHEN t1.week < 40 THEN 'DEC' 
                  WHEN t1.week < 45 THEN 'JAN' 
                  WHEN t1.week < 49 THEN 'FEB' 
                  WHEN t1.week < 53 THEN 'MAR' 
                  ELSE 'DEFAULT VALUE'
            END AS month, 
            dbo.inf_dates.months

FROM        dbo.[NonVoice Weekly_InflowCOMCAN] AS t1 
            INNER JOIN dbo.inf_dates 
                ON t1.week = dbo.inf_dates.fin_wk

WHERE       notes = 'Weekly COMPLETED'
            AND [2MB/sub]) = 'ETH' 
            AND dbo.inf_dates.date > CONVERT(datetime, '2017-04-03 00:00:00', 102)

GROUP BY   t1.region 
           ,dbo.inf_dates.months
